a:r.a:t: Whether [glucose] is high or low, if lactose is absent → repressor stays bound….→ no transcription even when CRP-cAMP bind.

p:cNvPr.descr: Part A: A four-part diagram, labeled a, b, c, and d, that illustrates the positive regulation of the lac operon by CRP. Part a shows a long, narrow rectangular structure divided into 13 segments, each separated by a short black line. Starting from the left to the right, the structure is labeled 5’, followed by a short blue segment, a short purple segment labeled P (subscript I), a pink segment labeled lacI, and an orange segment labeled O (subscript 3). To the right of O (subscript 3) is another short blue segment, followed by a purple segment labeled P, an orange segment labeled O (subscript I), and a tan segment labeled lacZ. To the right of lacZ is another orange segment labeled O (subscript 2), a short tan segment, a peach-colored segment labeled lacY, a yellow segment of the same size, labeled lacA, and a short blue segment; this entire chain ends with a 3’ on the right. The purple P and short blue segment next to it are shown, looped, so that P is pulled up on top. Below the looped section is a pink structure with four oddly-shaped tentacles attached to O (subscript 3) and O (subscript 1). The area at the bottom center of the loop is labeled CRP-binding site. Between P (subscript I) and lacI is an arrow that points down and right to bold green letters that say, “ON,” with a short curved arrow pointing away from it to the pink tentacles. Between O (subscript 1) and lacZ is a similar arrow pointing right to bold red letters that say, “OFF.” Below this, text reads, “No gene expression.” This is labeled as glucose high, cAMP low, lactose absent. Below this is part b, which shows the structure previously described, but this time a purple pentagon labeled cAMP and green boulder-like structure labeled CRP are lodged inside the loop at the top. This is labeled as glucose low, cAMP high, lactose absent. Below this is a similar structure, but now the loops are straightened out, so the light blue and P segments are part of the straight line. Before the light blue segment in the middle is a dark blue segment. Between O (subscript 1) and lacZ, the arrow now points to a lighter green ON, and below it, text reads, “Low level of gene expression.” An arrow below this text points to a wavy green line labeled as mRNA. An arrow below the first ON (on the left side of the structure) points down to the pink, tentacle structure, but it now has four gray, small boulders, two on each side, attached to it; these boulders are labeled as allolactose. A diagonal arrow points from the pink structure to O (subscript 1), and there’s a red X crossing the middle of the arrow. Below this structure is the same structure as just described, but this time, CRP and cAMP are sitting on top of the dark blue and light blue segments, next to RNA polymerase, which is a purple globular mass around the center of the rectangular structure. The “ON” between O (subscript 1) and lacZ is now the same dark green color as the one on the left, and below it, text reads, “High level of gene expression.” Below it, an arrow points down to mRNA, which is represented by five wavy green lines. Again, an arrow below the first ON (on the left side of the structure) points down to the pink, tentacle structure with the four gray, small boulders, and a diagonal arrow with a red X across the middle points up to O (subscript 1), where the RNA polymerase is lodged.
